page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.medium is an entry-level virtual server instance within the shared family, provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing two virtual CPUs backed by one physical core with two threads per core. The instance is allocated 4.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor architecture includes basic instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage, operating purely on network-attached storage, and does not feature GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects performance in lower tiers compared to modern cloud hardware. The instance scored 959.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1698.0 in Geekbench multi-core, with PassMark measuring an overall CPU score of 2676.41 and a memory score of 1127.43. Stress-ng returned 1108.59 for single-core and 2194.17 for multi-core tests. Memory throughput tests show 159.5 GB/sec for cached 16 KB small blocks, dropping to 16.3 GB/sec read and 14.46 GB/sec write for uncached 256 MB blocks. Application-level metrics show 2.87 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 1.9 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its single physical core and legacy processor architecture, the instance exhibits poor to weak throughput across compute-intensive, compression, and high-frequency database operations. It functions as a lightweight compute option suited for low-traffic web hosting, basic internal testing, small staging environments, or minor utility microservices that do not demand extensive CPU or memory bandwidth.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.medium is an entry-tier x86_64 instance featuring 2 vCPUs on a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPU hardware, relying on external network storage. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the lower percentiles across compute and memory metrics, recording a PassMark CPU score of 2676.41, a Geekbench multi-core score of 1698.0, and 2.87 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. The uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 16.3 GB/sec with write speeds of 14.46 GB/sec. Given its constrained core count and modest throughput profiles, ecs.n1.medium is best aligned with lightweight utility workloads, low-demand staging environments, and basic web serving rather than compute- or memory-intensive applications.
